sender.en: A “FedEx”, “DHL” or courier company executive, then “customs” or “cyber cell”

name.en: Courier parcel with drugs: “your parcel to Iran was seized by customs”

how.en: An automated call or a caller from a courier company says a parcel sent in your name, often to Iran, Thailand or Taiwan, was stopped by customs with drugs, fake passports or cash inside. The call is “transferred” to a police, narcotics or customs officer who accuses you of a crime, often on a video call. To avoid arrest you must pay a “fine”, “security deposit” or move money for “verification”. Courier firms do not connect you to the police, and officers do not settle cases over the phone.

text.en: A courier call says a parcel with your Aadhaar was seized with drugs or passports.
The call is transferred to a “police” or “narcotics” officer.
You are told the case is secret and you must not tell anyone.
They ask for a fee, fine or a transfer to clear your name.

Automated call: Your FedEx shipment has been held by customs. Press 1 to speak to an executive. Executive: The parcel booked with your Aadhaar to Tehran contains five passports and MDMA. I am connecting you to Mumbai Narcotics for your statement; please stay on the line.
